chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Atiyya, from Khaysama, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, Allah is distinct from His creation, and His creation is distinct from Him; and everything upon which the name 'thing' applies, apart from Allah the Exalted, is a created thing, and Allah is the Creator of everything.

key_terms.خَالِق: Creator — the One who brings all things into existence
key_terms.خَلْق: Creation — the totality of everything God has brought into existence
key_terms.خِلْوٌ: Distinct, separate, free from — used here to express God's absolute transcendence and ontological separation from creation
key_terms.شَيْء: Thing — any entity that can be named or categorized; everything except God falls under this category as a created being
key_terms.مَخْلُوق: Created thing, creature — anything brought into existence by God

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about God's relationship to creation in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) articulates a core Shia theological principle: the absolute ontological separation between God and creation. God is not a 'thing' in the way creatures are things; everything that can be called a 'thing' — except God — is created. This hadith, narrated in the context of debates about divine attributes, establishes that God transcends all categories applicable to creatures, including the very category of 'thing' (shay'). The original audience — students of theology in the early Shia tradition — understood this as a refutation of anthropomorphism and as affirming God's utter transcendence.
